'''John Anthony Pojman''' (born May 29, 1962) is an American [[chemist]] and professor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Narveson |first=Deanna B. |date=2015-08-19 |title=An LSU professor has invented a curious clay with a range of applications, from art to industry. |url=https://www.businessreport.com/business/lsu-professor-invented-curious-clay-range-applications-art-industry |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=Baton Rouge Business Report |language=en-US}}</ref> He is known for researching frontal polymerization, nonlinear chemical dynamics, and polymeric systems.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2016-04-28 |title=LSU professor's QuickCure Clay can fix anything from a wooden floor to your cat's neck |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/entertainment_life/lsu-professor-s-quickcure-clay-can-fix-anything-from-a-wooden-floor-to-your-cat/article_5ea3d502-b2c5-520d-9709-83054b2f4bff.html |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=The Advocate |language=en}}</ref> He is the Patricia Senn and William Senn, Jr., Distinguished Professor and Chair of the Department of Chemistry at [[Louisiana State University]] (LSU) and the founder of Pojman Polymer Products, LLC.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-05-12 |title=Dr. Pojman pioneers new formula for mold-making |url=http://neworleansglassworks.com/dr-pojman-pioneers-new-formula-for-mold-making/ |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=New Orleans Glassworks & Printmaking Studio |language=en}}</ref> His work has applications in [[materials science]], [[3D printing|additive manufacturing]], and [[Weightlessness|microgravity]] polymer processing.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Science In Orbit |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/88/i5/Science-Orbit.html |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=Chemical & Engineering News |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Pojman was born in [[Cleveland, Ohio]], and raised in [[North Royalton]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Dr. John Pojman {{!}} The Space Show |url=https://www.thespaceshow.com/guest/dr.-john-pojman |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=www.thespaceshow.com}}</ref> He earned a B.S. in Chemistry with a minor in Classics from [[Georgetown University]] in 1984.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pojman Research Team |url=https://faculty.lsu.edu/pojman/people.php |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=faculty.lsu.edu}}</ref> He completed his doctorate in Chemical Physics at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in 1988<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stanley |first=S |date=2019-03-20 |title=John Pojman to Present Physics Lecture March 29 |url=https://wooster.edu/2019/03/20/john-pojman-to-present-physics-lecture-march-29/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240817041158/https://wooster.edu/2019/03/20/john-pojman-to-present-physics-lecture-march-29/ |archive-date=2024-08-17 |access-date=2025-03-07 |work=The College of Wooster |language=en-US}}</ref> under the supervision of Nobel laureate [[Ilya Prigogine]] and James Whitesell.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kondepudi |first1=Dilip |last2=Petrosky |first2=Tomio |last3=Pojman |first3=John A. |date=2017-10-01 |title=Dissipative structures and irreversibility in nature: Celebrating 100th birth anniversary of Ilya Prigogine (1917–2003) |url=https://pubs.aip.org/cha/article/27/10/104501/151553/Dissipative-structures-and-irreversibility-in |journal=Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science |language=en |volume=27 |issue=10 |doi=10.1063/1.5008858 |pmid=29092431 |bibcode=2017Chaos..27j4501K |issn=1054-1500|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Pojman conducted postdoctoral research at [[Brandeis University]] with Irving Epstein from 1988 to 1990.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=John A Pojman shares his journey to a chemical career |url=https://www.lsu.edu/academicaffairs/cxc/news/2018/lsuexperimental_15.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240727060921/https://www.lsu.edu/academicaffairs/cxc/news/2018/lsuexperimental_15.php |archive-date=2024-07-27 |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=www.lsu.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Pojman began his academic career at the [[University of Southern Mississippi]] (USM) in 1990.<ref name=":1" /> He started his career as an [[assistant professor]] and was promoted to full professor by 1997.<ref name=":2" /> He joined [[Louisiana State University|LSU]] in 2008 as a professor and became chair of the [[Chemistry]] Department in 2020.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Pojman Receives 2023 Charles E. Coates Memorial Award – LAMDA |url=https://lamda.rsi.laregents.edu/pojman-receives-2023-charles-e-coates-memorial-award/ |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=lamda.rsi.laregents.edu}}</ref> His research focuses on [[Nonlinear system|nonlinear]] phenomena in [[polymer]]s, including frontal [[polymerization]]—a self-propagating reaction process he pioneered for rapid material curing.<ref name=":0" /> This work led to developing commercial products such as QuickCure Clay and QuickCure Wood Filler, licensed through his company, Pojman Polymer Products, LLC.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-01-29 |title=LSU Innovation Park company licenses QuickCure Clay; 3 new companies enter tech park |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/news/business/lsu-innovation-park-company-licenses-quickcure-clay-3-new-companies-enter-tech-park/article_a44dfdde-051a-11e8-85a9-3f1925e27f68.html |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=The Advocate |language=en}}</ref>

He has collaborated with NASA on microgravity experiments, including studies aboard the KC-135 aircraft and contributions to projects on the [[International Space Station]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=August 2011 |title=Commercial space flight: Scientists in space |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nj7361-477a |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=476 |issue=7361 |pages=477–478 |doi=10.1038/nj7361-477a |issn=1476-4687 |last1=Sanderson |first1=Katharine |pmid=21870357 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He personally flew over 800 parabolas on NASA's KC-135 microgravity research plane.<ref>{{Cite web |title=kc135 reduced gravity: Topics by Science.gov |url=https://www.science.gov/topicpages/k/kc135+reduced+gravity |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=www.science.gov}}</ref> He also developed an experiment that flew on the Blue Origins suborbital rocket.  Pojman has organized symposia on nonlinear dynamics and polymer science for the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS) and [[Gordon Research Conferences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chemistry experiment aboard historic suborbital space flight |url=https://phys.org/news/2016-06-chemistry-aboard-historic-suborbital-space.html#google_vignette |website=phys,org}}</ref>

He also co-curated an exhibit on “''Polymers in Art through the centuries''” at the [[Louisiana Art and Science Museum]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Robin |date=2017-07-29 |title=LASM's exhibit explores the mix of art and science |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/entertainment_life/arts/lasms-exhibit-explores-the-mix-of-art-and-science/article_c5245630-716c-11e7-9285-dfce393ee328.html |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=The Advocate |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, he received the Charles E. Coates Memorial Award, Baton Rouge ACS/AIChE.<ref name=":3" />

== Research ==
Pojman's research spans frontal polymerization, cure-on-demand systems, time-lapse polymerizations, chemo-[[Fluid dynamics|hydrodynamic]] instabilities and the materials of art.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pojman |first1=John |last2=Gunn |first2=Grady |last3=Patterson |first3=Chilibra |last4=Omens |first4=Jim |last5=Simmons |first5=Chris |date=1998-05-01 |title=Frontal Dispersion Polymerization |url=https://aquila.usm.edu/fac_pubs/4973/ |journal=Journal of Physical Chemistry B |volume=102 |issue=20 |pages=3927–3929|doi=10.1021/jp9814911 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> His work on miscible fluid interactions in [[Weightlessness|microgravity]] addressed long-standing questions in [[fluid dynamics]]. He has published over 185 peer-reviewed articles and co-authored ''An Introduction to Nonlinear Chemical Dynamics'' ([[Oxford University Press]]).<ref>{{Cite web |title=An Introduction to Nonlinear Chemical Dynamics |url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/an-introduction-to-nonlinear-chemical-dynamics-9780195096705 |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=global.oup.com}}</ref> His cure-on-demand polymer processing innovations, based on frontal polymerization, have been applied to arts and crafts materials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pocket Protector Professor |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/87/i33/Pocket-Protector-Professor.html |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=Chemical & Engineering News |language=en}}</ref>

Pojman's development of QuickCure Clay, a sculpting material that hardens rapidly via heat-activated frontal polymerization, has been used in artistic applications such as repairing [[ceramic]]s and creating textured paintings.<ref name=":0" /> He is an inventor on 6 patents.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ross |first=Kenya |date=2023-05-10 |title=LSU and LSU AgCenter develop patent-pending bait to control wild hog population |url=https://www.knoe.com/2023/05/10/lsu-lsu-agcenter-develop-patent-pending-bait-control-wild-hog-population/ |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=[[KNOE-TV]] |language=en}}</ref> Pojman is a co-inventor of a [[Feral pig|feral hog]] toxicant.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-03-02 |title=Finding the right bait to reduce the feral hog problem |url=https://www.rfdtv.com/finding-the-right-bait-to-reduce-the-feral-hog-problem |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=RFD-TV |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosato |first=Chris |date=2023-03-07 |title=Wild pig-fighting bait developed by LSU |url=https://www.wafb.com/2023/03/07/wild-pig-fighting-bait-developed-by-lsu/ |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=[[WAFB]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal ==

Pojman lives in Baton Rouge, Louisiana with his wife, Dionne M. Rousseau.

==Awards==
*2023: Charles E. Coates Memorial Award.<ref name=":3" />
*2023:Southwest Regional ACS Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LSU Chemistry professor receives Southwest Regional ACS Award |url=https://www.lsu.edu/science/chemistry/news/2023/oct/pojman_swrm-award.php |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=www.lsu.edu}}</ref>
*2025:Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=LSU Chemistry Professor Named AAAS Fellow for Contributions to Polymer Science |url=https://www.lsu.edu/science/chemistry/news/2025/mar/pojman-aaas.php |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=www.lsu.edu}}</ref>
